filters.question: Does it explicitly describe the use of thermal pretreatment on a substrate (e.g., microwave, hydrothermal treatment, steam explosion, autoclave)
filters.reasoning: Reasoning: The question asks whether the methodology section explicitly describes thermal pretreatment, specifically hydrothermal treatment, on a substrate. Let's examine the methodology section closely. It details the HTP process as follows: “The HTP process was conducted in a 1000 mL stainless-steel autoclave reactor (WZC-1000, WZC, Beijing, China) with a Teflon lining inside. The total volatile solids (VS) concentration in the reactor was 30 g VS·L^−1. According to the pre-experimental results, the FW-to-Enteromorpha ratio was 3:1 on a VS basis. Based of the results of a previous study [23], the addition amount of oyster shells was 8% (w/w) of total dry weight of FW and Enteromorpha, to strengthen the system, stabilize pH, and improve the performance of DF [23-25]. The moisture content of the HTP process was set at 90%, which was adjusted by adding deionized water. The reactor was heated to the desired temperature (50, 80, 110, or 140 °C) and maintained for 20 min. The HTP time was precisely measured, starting at the time the reactor reached the set temperature. After the HTP process, the reactor was cooled to 25 °C using tap water, and the pretreated substrates were removed for subsequent analyses and digestion trials.” This clearly describes a hydrothermal pretreatment process using an autoclave, involving heating the substrates to specific temperatures for a defined period.
